notes: Loop 1, first verdict (no earlier file). Rebuilt the demo by hand: deal €6.30, lunch €7.616, switching 11.4 × €1.316 = €15.0024/day, running €23/day, break-even (15.0024+23+18)/6.30 = 8.89 → 9 (ongoing 7), scenarios −€371 / −€56.02 / +€385, worst case −€560 (37% of €1,500), tornado €756/260/210/200; price: −9.2%, 57 cups, +€210.80, −€111.60, rule 563/535. Every value is right, so no hard cap. Strong: one model per template with its formulas in the header (lunch-offer.ts:1-15), maths strings in the owner's numbers, an independent re-statement in the tests and exact break-even variants (engine.test.ts 'break-even is exact'), a monotonic slider, plain refusals (deal at cost). Held back: (1) the test card's rounded thresholds and compareResult's exact ones disagree, so the verdict flips at the edges; (2) several maths strings do not reproduce their value: the headline −€56.02 against 12.40 × 10 − 180 = −56.00, '11.4 × €1.32 = €15.00' (that is €15.05), '+€105 × 14 ÷ 7 = +€211'; (3) 'the most it can cost' depends on the 30% switching guess; (4) inputs off the demo path give silent nonsense; the tests miss all four.
improvements: Correctness, rounding flips the verdict. src/engine/compare.ts:464-469 judges the result against the exact break-even (keep from 8.89, tweak from 4.44), but the test card from src/engine/experiment.ts:68 and :106-111 prints 'At least 9 … keep', '5 to 8 tweak', 'Fewer than 5 stop' and tells the owner to 'agree it now'. If the owner logs 4.5 extra a day, the engine says 'tweak' after the card said stop. At 8.9 it says 'the test needed 9 extra a day … So the verdict is: keep the deal'. The price template has the same gap: 534.5 a week gives 'tweak' while the card says 'fewer than 535: stop' (compare.ts:529-533 against experiment.ts:175-177). Fix: one decisionThresholds(model) in the engine that both planTest and compareResult call. Test: on a grid of x values, compareResult's verdict always matches the printed rule.

Transparency, the maths strings must reproduce their values. The report's headline tile shows −€56.02 (report.txt, 'Your likely guess, over the 10-day test'), but its working '+€12.40 × 10 weekdays − €180 setup = −€56.02' works out to −€56.00. In the same way, '11.4 × €1.32 = €15.00' is €15.05, the slider at 9 a day gives '+€18.70 a day … +€6.98' (that is +€7.00), and in the price template '+€105 × 14 ÷ 7 = +€211' (210), '+€105 × 4.33 = +€456' (455) and '€1,773 − €1,829 now = −€55.80' (−56). The fix is in one place: round the per-lunch margin to cents inside lunchModel (lunch-offer.ts:123), or print operands at the precision the model uses. Keep cents on intermediates in price-change.ts:133-137. Also align skill/what-if/references/maths.md:180 (52 ÷ 12, which gives €456.73) with WEEKS_PER_MONTH = 4.33 (€456.38). Test: parse every Figure.maths of the form 'a × b − c = d' and assert it holds within display precision.

Honesty, a guess-dependent ceiling is presented as a fact. 'That is the most it can cost' (lunch-offer.ts:301), 'the whole test cannot cost more than €560' (experiment.ts:136) and the tile tagged 'Calculated' all assume the guessed 30% of regulars switch. With switch_share 1 the same no-new-customers test costs €910. Say: 'If nobody new comes and about 11 regulars a day switch, as you guessed, the test costs €560; if every lunch regular switched it could reach €910'. Also, the €370 stop line includes €75 of margin lost to switching regulars (experiment.ts:65), but the card's 'Money spent' step only collects receipts (€295 by day 5), so the owner cannot apply it. Give the cash line and the margin line separately.

Edge cases that now give silent nonsense. (a) inputs.ts:105 caps the derived optimistic guess at +5%. A price cut with only 'likely +10%' is refused with 'The optimistic guess is below the likely guess; swap them', about a number the owner never gave; use max(likely, …). (b) With no change in sales, price-change.ts:204 prints 'Whether sales change by 0% or 0% changes the test result by €0 — more than anything else'. (c) A current price below cost gives break-even −120%, and the card says 'you still sell at least -124 a week' and 'fewer than -496' (experiment.ts:175-184); clamp at −100%. (d) Break-even 0 gives 'stop early if you have spent €10 without reaching 0 a day … cannot cost more than €0' (experiment.ts:136-137). (e) There are no plausibility warnings: extra_likely 200 against 140 customers a day and 38 at lunch reads 'the test pays for itself', and a deal 1 cent above cost needs 12,771 extra a day yet still gets a card that says 'tweak: 6386 to 12770 a day'. Warn when a guess or the break-even exceeds today's lunch or day count. When the break-even is far beyond the optimistic guess, give 'do not test as it stands'.

Tests should pin the invariants, not only the demo. test/engine.test.ts pins the demo values and the break-even exactly, but nothing in it catches items 1, 2 or 4. Add: maths-reproduces-value for every Figure; card rule equal to the compareResult verdict; a seeded property test over random valid inputs (no NaN, no negative counts in any text, no 'X or X', worst ≤ every scenario); and named cases for price with no lost sales, a price cut with only the likely guess, a price below cost, break-even 0 and lunch_customers 0.

Code, one formula in one place. The helpers n, has, ceilUp, pc, eur and seur are copied into lunch-offer.ts, price-change.ts, experiment.ts and compare.ts. comparePrice recomputes the weekly delta (compare.ts:525) instead of calling priceModel. The report computes money itself: 'compared with your guess' is p.netTest − gp.netTest at src/report/sections.ts:273. format.ts holds the currency as module-level mutable state, set as a side effect by analyze, planTest and compareResult. Move the helpers into format.ts, add the delta to SensitivityPoint and pass the currency explicitly.
